# [TASK] Stop holding a DB connection across the ai-service model call, and bound it

## Task

Three defects around how the model call consumes resources.

**The LLM call runs inside a database transaction.** `ChatAssistantService.chat` is `@Transactional` and blocks on `chatClient…call()` in the middle of it, so a PostgreSQL connection is held from the Hikari pool for the full model round-trip rather than only for the reads and writes that need one. `RecommendationService.recommend` is worse: it holds the transaction across both the movie-service HTTP call and the LLM call. With Hikari's default pool of 10, a modest number of concurrent chat requests exhausts the pool, and every other DB-touching request — including the actuator health check's DB probe — then blocks on connection acquisition until a model call returns.

**The intended 60s LLM timeout does not exist.** `spring.ai.ollama.chat.options.timeout` is not a real property in Spring AI 2.0.0: `OllamaChatProperties` flattens its properties directly under `spring.ai.ollama.chat` (`.model`, `.temperature`, `.num-ctx`, …), has no `options` prefix, and has no `timeout` field at all — confirmed against `spring-ai-autoconfigure-model-ollama-2.0.0`'s `spring-configuration-metadata.json`. `@ConfigurationProperties` defaults to `ignoreUnknownFields = true`, so the binding silently no-ops with no startup warning. If Ollama hangs or is still loading a model, the request waits on the underlying client's default read timeout — while holding the DB connection above. The operator believes a 60s ceiling exists; it does not.

**Conversation history is re-sent whole on every turn.** `chat()` loads every message ever written to the conversation and sends all of them, with no windowing, truncation, or token budget. Turn N sends O(N) history, so a conversation's total token cost grows quadratically. Past roughly 30–60 turns (model-dependent) the prompt exceeds `llama3.2`'s context window; Ollama then truncates from the front — dropping the system prompt, which shares that window — or errors, and every subsequent turn in that conversation fails permanently with no recovery short of starting a new conversation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] No DB connection is held across the LLM call or the movie-service call — transactions cover only the persistence work
- [x] A real, configurable timeout bounds the model call, set through a property that Spring AI actually binds (verified against the property metadata, not assumed)
- [x] Conversation history sent to the model is windowed or token-budgeted, so a long conversation neither drops the system prompt nor becomes permanently unusable
- [x] A test proves a long conversation still succeeds past the turn count that previously broke it
